biology.blood-ext.0014.all: Vaccine contains dead/inactive/weakened polio virus (antigens); antigens recognised by lymphocytes; lymphocytes divide and produce specific antibodies; memory cells formed; on later infection memory cells respond faster, more antibodies produced, more quickly; virus destroyed before symptoms; immunity.

biology.bubbles.0005.all: 89 anomalous; mean of 35 and 40 = 37.5 bubbles in 3 min; 37.5/3 = 12.5 bubbles per minute

biology.crops-data-pct.0003.b: Fertiliser provides nitrate ions; absorbed by roots (active transport); used to make amino acids/proteins for growth; more growth/more photosynthesis so higher yield

biology.crops-prac-method.0002.all: Use several masses of fertiliser (e.g. 0, 5, 10, 15 g) in same volume/mass of compost; same variety/age of plants, same pot size, light, temperature, water; several plants per mass; grow for fixed time; harvest and weigh tomatoes per plant; calculate mean.

biology.crops-prac-risk.0002.a: Fertiliser is an irritant/harmful if ingested or on skin; wear gloves and wash hands
biology.crops-prac-risk.0002.b: Use a balance with greater resolution/top-pan balance; dry tomatoes; weigh all tomatoes from each plant and repeat for several plants

biology.cycles-ext.0004.all: Burning: combustion of wood releases CO2 directly; Fewer trees so less photosynthesis, less CO2 removed; remaining wood/roots decomposed by microorganisms which respire releasing CO2; carbon no longer stored in trees; net increase in atmospheric CO2; contributes to greenhouse effect/global warming.

biology.environment-prac-plan.0002.all: Lay tape measure from hedge into field (transect); place quadrat at regular intervals e.g. every 1 m; count number of plants or % cover in each quadrat; repeat with several transects; control/keep same quadrat size, same time; measure abiotic factors such as light intensity; plot abundance vs distance.

biology.environment-prac-reliab.0003.a: To identify anomalous results and calculate a mean, making the results more reliable/repeatable
biology.environment-prac-reliab.0003.b: e.g. height on shore / time of tide / exposure to waves; sample at same height on shore/same time relative to low tide (or same quadrat size)

biology.environment-prac-risk.0002.a: Tripping over tape measure / uneven ground / allergens or stinging plants; take care, wear suitable footwear, wear gloves
biology.environment-prac-risk.0002.b: Use quadrat divided into grid of small squares (e.g. 100) and count squares covered; same person estimating

biology.excretion-ext.0010.all: Blood enters glomerulus under high pressure; ultrafiltration of small molecules (water, glucose, urea, salts) into Bowman's capsule; proteins/cells stay in blood; in proximal convoluted tubule all glucose selectively reabsorbed (active transport); loop of Henle; water reabsorbed in collecting duct under control of ADH; remaining urea, excess water and salts form urine to ureter/bladder.

biology.feeding-data-read.0004.a: Read from graph (graph not visible in text; values cannot be determined)
biology.feeding-data-read.0004.b: (value at 5 weeks - value at 1 week)/4 aphids per week
biology.feeding-data-read.0004.c: Ladybirds are predators that eat aphids; so aphid numbers fall; fewer aphids then limit ladybird food (or aphids reproduce initially before predation)

biology.homeostasis-ext.0004.all: Homeostasis keeps internal conditions constant for enzymes/cells to function; temperature kept ~37 C, optimum for enzymes, too high denatures, too low slows reactions; controlled by hypothalamus, sweating, vasodilation/constriction, shivering; water content: prevents cells losing/gaining water by osmosis (crenation/bursting); kidney/ADH regulates.

biology.human-nutrition-data-graph.0001.a: As time increases starch concentration decreases; rapid at first then slows; levels off at/near zero (values unreadable from text)
biology.human-nutrition-data-graph.0001.b: Amylase digests/breaks down starch into maltose; at first lots of substrate so many collisions/enzyme-substrate complexes; as starch used up rate falls; 37 C near optimum

biology.human-nutrition-data-plot.0003.a: Axes: age (x), energy (y) with labels/units, suitable scale; points plotted correctly; smooth curve
biology.human-nutrition-data-plot.0003.b: Energy requirement increases with age up to 18 years (max 10800 kJ); increase from 4320 at 2 to 10800 at 18; then decreases slightly to 10350 at 30

biology.human-nutrition-prac-plan.0001.all: Measure fixed volume of water (e.g. 20 cm3) into boiling tube, record start temperature; weigh food sample; ignite with Bunsen and hold under tube until it burns out; relight if needed; record final temperature; energy = mass water x 4.2 x temp rise / mass food; same volume water, same distance; repeat for each food, calculate mean.

biology.nervous-data-plot.0002.a: Axes labelled with units, sensible scale; points plotted; smooth curve
biology.nervous-data-plot.0002.b: As light intensity increases pupil diameter decreases; rapidly at first (6.5 to 3.2 by 30) then more slowly; levels off at about 2.1 mm

biology.nervous-data-read.0001.c: Reflex; circular muscles of iris contract; radial muscles relax; pupil constricts in bright light to protect retina

biology.plant-nutrition-ext.0015.all: Nitrate ions for amino acids/proteins for growth; magnesium needed to make chlorophyll; lack of magnesium means less chlorophyll; leaves yellow (chlorosis) especially between veins/older leaves; less light absorbed so less photosynthesis; less glucose so poor growth; ions absorbed by root hair cells by active transport.

biology.plant-nutrition-prac-reliab.0003.a: To identify anomalies and calculate a mean so results are more reliable
biology.plant-nutrition-prac-reliab.0003.b: Pondweed in water with no sodium hydrogencarbonate (or boiled/dead pondweed); to show oxygen production is due to the hydrogencarbonate/CO2 (or photosynthesis by living plant)

biology.plant-nutrition-recall-multi.000.a: Light intensity; carbon dioxide concentration; temperature

biology.plant-reproduction-data-graph.00.a: Germination increases with temperature to an optimum (about 25-30 C) then decreases at higher temperatures (graph values not visible)
biology.plant-reproduction-data-graph.00.b: Enzymes needed for germination; low temp less kinetic energy, slower enzyme activity; optimum; high temp enzymes denature so germination falls

biology.plant-responses-prac-plan.0001.all: Grow seedlings (e.g. cress) of same type/age in dishes; place one set in box with slit on one side (unilateral light), control in all-round light or darkness; same temperature, water, time; leave several days; measure angle of curvature/length of shoots; use many seedlings and repeat; shoots bend towards light (phototropism).

biology.plant-responses-prac-step.0001.all: Seedlings vary/some may not germinate or be anomalous; using ten allows a mean to be calculated, making results more reliable/representative

biology.respiration-prac-plan.0003.all: Mix yeast with glucose/sugar solution in tube; delivery tube into limewater (or hydrogencarbonate indicator); keep in water bath at e.g. 30-35 C; control tube with boiled yeast or no yeast; same volumes/concentration; observe limewater turning milky/cloudy; time how long it takes; repeat.
